Commentary.Commentary: Right then! Two exciting games so far and already heads are turning to see what this Bangladesh-England series is all about. Can we expect another humdinger in the third? Join us for the final ODI on Wednesday, 12th October, 2016 at 0830 GMT (1400 IST). Adios! Take Care!

Victorious Bangladesh skipper, MASHRAFE MORTAZA IS THE MAN OF THE MATCH AS WELL. He is happy with the win and congratulates his team. He says they were always confident that they could defend 240 but also praises his team's bowling. Admits that they were unprofessional in the first game but much profesonal tonight. On his batting, he says, he just swung at the ball and was lucky to get some runs. Is happy that he could pick up wickets for his side. Feels that if you lose 2-3 wickets early, then 240 could be difficult to chase. Is raring to play the final game and says that the whole side is up for it as it is a big match for them.

England captain, JOS BUTTLER is disappointed with the way of the defeat rather than the loss itself. He feels the batsmen were tentative in approaching the target which is not the way this English team plays. Says that 239 was chaseable if the batsmen had applied themselves. On the controversy surrounding his dismissal, he says that he was just unhappy with the way Bangladesh players celebrated but also admits that such things happen in the heat of the moment. Praises his bowlers for bowling well and does not look too much into the carnage in the death. Lauds his side for bowling well in both games. Admits that they were confident of going 2-0 up tonight but the conditions were tough. Does not want to look too much into this defeat and feels it was a blip. Opines that 240 can be chased down in two ways - either you chase it in in 42 overs or take it till the 50th - he prefers to do it in 42. Further says he prefers being 60/3 after 10 overs rather than 20/3.

The hosts perhaps took it easy after Woakes got out as they struggled to pick up the last two wickets. But eventually, they got the job done. Skipper Mortaza led from the front with 4 wickets while Taskin Ahmed changed the game in his second spell where he picked up 4 wickets for 12 runs in 19 balls. Nasir Hossain was extremely economical on return. Stay tuned for the presentation...

239 was not the easiest of targets to chase and after losing 4 quickly, England were in desperate trouble. Skipper Mortaza had run through the top order and left the side reeling. Bairstow and Buttler then revided the innings with a 79-run stand but once that was broken, another collapse ensued.
The series is alive and kicking. The crowd was heartbroken on Friday night as it saw a match slip right under its noses. But tonight, its team has stood up and delivered the goods.

On middle and leg, played straight to short mid-wicket.
BEN DUCKETT walks in at number 3, replacing Vince.

OUT! Caught! Bangladesh strike early! Loose from Vince. It wasa full ball and wide outside off and deservedly should have been put away. But he does not move his feet and plays a loose shot. The ball is aerial and straight to Mosaddek Hossain at point who did not make any mistake. ENGLAND NEED 227 FROM 278 BALLS.
Played to the point region by the batsman.
Outside off, Vince feels for it but then tries to withdraw his bat. Is late and gets beaten.
On middle, flicked through mid-wicket for a single.
Full and outside off, this is quietly defended.
FOUR! LUCKY! Full and wide outside off, Vicne reaches out, trying to drive and gets a thick outside edge which flies over point to third man! 228 more needed from 283 balls now.
Full on middle, clipped through mid-wicket for a single.
The batsman gets an inside edge and the ball hits him on the pads.
NOT OUT. Nicely bowled, tossed up outside off, Roy is drawn into the drive but is beaten. Rahim whips off the bails and appeals and it is taken upstairs. Replays show that Roy never left the crease.
STUMPING APPEAL! Is Roy in trouble? Referred upstairs...
Full and around off, Roy lunges to defend but gets a thick inside edge onto his pads. Nearly rolls back onto the stumps!

RUN OUT CHANCE MISSED! Lucky escape. On middle, Vince works it through mid-wicket and sets off for a single but Roy does not move. The striker has to return but Vince gives it up. The fielder picks up the ball and has a shy at the striker's end but misses. Vince was a goner.
Full and outside off, Roy drives this down the ground but it deflects off the non-striker's bat wide of mid on who has to run around to stop the ball. A single taken.
On middle and leg, worked through mid-wicket for a single.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Outside off, angling in, Vince looks to tuck it to the leg side but gets a thick inside edge onto his pads.
Full and outside off, driven back to the bowler.
MASHRAFE MORTAZA to bowl with the second new ball.

HUGE LBW SHOUT! Turned down. The arm ball around off, darting in, Roy stayed back to defend but missed and was hit on the pads. Hawk Eye showed the ball to be going over the top.
